before.b:

before.ti: Water table depth: every CS456 datum is wrong, and the offset lives in the logger
before.b:
The sign convention is settled. AmeriFlux's measurement-height page states that "positive values are heights, and negative values are depths", so for WTD: positive = water above the surface, negative = below it. That is the sign the CR1000X already produces: Lvl_m = Lvl_psi*0.70307 - WTD_offset, where the first term is the height of water above the transducer and WTD_offset is the sensor's depth below the surface. The logger's arithmetic was never the problem.

The offsets were. Not one of the four sites had a datum that survives contact with a tape measure, and each is wrong in a different way:

SiteOffset in the cal fileWhat that impliesTrue sensor depth
UQAM_20.79 mwater 1.1 m above an open bog, all season2.05 m (measured)
UQAM_30.00 → 1.75 → 1.48 mthree different datums in one season, none right1.83 m
UQAM_4−1.57 mwater 2.9 m above a drained peatland3.15 m (disputed)
McGill_11.58 m0.8 m of water below the bed, at an open-water site under a metre of it−0.16 m

Two problems follow from applying the offset inside the logger. First, only the corrected value carries meaning and nothing records which offset was in force on which date: the history above had to be recovered by differencing the archived Lvl_psi_Avg against Lvl_m_Avg. Second, an offset can be tuned to agree with a field tape at exactly one instant and still be wrong everywhere else, which is what happened at UQAM_3 on 10 June.

Barometric compensation was suspected and is not the problem: the CS456 is a vented gauge sensor and aM1! returns psig. Regressing 30-minute changes in head against 30-minute changes in station pressure gives a slope within 0.01 m/kPa of zero at both bog sites, against +0.102 for a sensor with no vent compensation.
before.fix: Change the logger line to publish raw head only (Lvl_m = Lvl_psi*0.70307) and apply the datum in first stage as a dated calibration: currentCalibration = [0.70307 -<sensor_depth_below_surface> datenum(start) datenum(2999,12,31)]. A negative depth is legitimate where the sensor hangs above the bed, as at McGill_1. That makes a datum correction retroactive and reviewable instead of stamping a step into the record, and since Lvl_psi_Avg is archived everywhere the whole 2026 season can be rebuilt without losing anything. after.ti: Water table depth: every CS456 datum is wrong, and the offset lives in the logger
after.b:
The sign convention is settled. AmeriFlux's measurement-height page states that "positive values are heights, and negative values are depths", so for WTD: positive = water above the surface, negative = below it. That is the sign the CR1000X already produces: Lvl_m = Lvl_psi*0.70307 - WTD_offset, where the first term is the height of water above the transducer and WTD_offset is the sensor's depth below the surface. The logger's arithmetic was never the problem.

The offsets were. Not one of the four sites had a datum that survives contact with a tape measure, and each is wrong in a different way:

SiteOffset in the cal fileWhat that impliesTrue sensor depth
UQAM_20.79 mwater 1.1 m above an open bog, all season2.05 m (measured)
UQAM_30.00 → 1.75 → 1.48 mthree different datums in one season, none right1.83 m
UQAM_4−1.57 mwater 2.9 m above a drained peatland2.60 m (measured 2026-11-11)
McGill_11.58 m0.8 m of water below the bed, at an open-water site under a metre of it−0.16 m

Barometric compensation was suspected and is not the problem: the CS456 is a vented gauge sensor and aM1! returns psig. Regressing 30-minute changes in head against 30-minute changes in station pressure gives a slope within 0.01 m/kPa of zero at both bog sites, against +0.102 for a sensor with no vent compensation.

Datum settled on 2026-11-11. Tie-in at 11:54 EST: 1.7053 psi with the water 1.40 m below the ground. The pipe is 3.15 m long with 2.65 m in the ground (0.50 m above it), so 3.15 m was the pipe length. Sensor depth = 1.40 + 1.7053 × 0.70307 = 2.60 m below the ground, 5 cm above the pipe bottom and inside the 2.70 m hole. The reading before and after the visit is the same (1.7105 and 1.7147 psi), so the sensor went back to the same depth and the datum applies to the whole record: the season runs −1.65 to −1.00 m, wettest in early August, −1.40 m on Nov 11.
after.fix:
Source WTD_1_1_1 from Lvl_psi_Avg with currentCalibration = [0.70307 -2.60 datenum(2026,5,15) datenum(2999,12,31)], starting the trace on 2026-05-16. Widen minMax to [-2.6 0.5]: with the new datum the old upper limit of −1.2 would delete 2009 good half hours, mostly in August. Remove the visit half hours 2026-11-11 12:00 and 12:30 EST. Until the logger publishes raw head only, ignore Lvl_m_Avg (the cal file still holds −1.57).

How WTD is calculated from the logger pressure. The CS456 is a vented gauge sensor, so Lvl_psi_Avg is the pressure of the water column above it. In first stage:
WTD [m] = Lvl_psi_Avg × 0.70307 − d
where 0.70307 m/psi converts pressure to metres of water (1000 kg/m³, 9.80665 m/s²) and d is the depth of the sensor below the ground. d comes from a manual tie-in: d = water depth below the ground (tape) + psi read at that moment × 0.70307. On 2026-11-11: 1.40 + 1.7053 × 0.70307 = 2.60 m. Biomet.net applies currentCalibration = [gain offset start end] as value × gain + offset, so the trace carries [0.70307 -2.60 ...]. Negative values are below the surface. Each new tie-in (for example after the spring reinstallation, see pn19) becomes a new dated currentCalibration row.

before.ti: Open water measured against a datum 1.7 m out
before.period: All data to date; CS456 from 2026-05-28
before.b:
McGill_1 is open water. Its CS456 is a stage sensor reading the depth of the water column over the lake bed, not a well in soil: there is no unsaturated zone, so the value is positive all season by construction and the sign convention never bites here. The datum does.

Two faults. First, WTD_1_1_1 was sourced from L_WATER_Avg, the EasyProbe level channel, with no date limit, so the pre-CS456 record is EasyProbe level standing in for water depth. Second, since the CS456 was added on 28 May the cal file has carried WTD_offset = 1.58 m, which reports 0.73 to 0.88 m of water below the bed at a site standing under about a metre of it: out by roughly 1.7 m.

At installation there was 0.87 m of water above the bed and head averaged 0.7109 m, so the transducer sits 0.16 m above the bed, on its mount in the water column. Its depth relative to the reference surface is therefore negative. That is the normal case for a stage sensor and not a sign error: the arithmetic is unchanged, WTD = head − depth, so a negative depth adds rather than subtracts. Corrected, the season runs +0.87 to +1.01 m: a lake level creeping up about 14 cm through the summer.

before.flag: Three things. (1) The installation was reported as reading 1.1265 psi, but the archive holds 1.0098–1.0133 psi across the whole of 28 May and does not exceed 1.10 psi before 2 July; the archived value is used here, and if 1.1265 psi is right the depth becomes −0.08 m instead, an 8 cm difference. (2) The field note reasons that "values are negative because the water sits above ground: this is correct". Under the AmeriFlux convention that is backwards: water above the surface is positive. WTD is defined as water table depth and this is a surface-water stage measurement; wetland sites commonly report standing water under WTD as a positive value, which is what is done here, but if AmeriFlux has a dedicated surface-water variable it belongs there. before.ti: Deepest soil profile probe: 45 cm or 64 cm?
before.b:
UQAM_2_FirstStage.ini states that the deepest CS650 in the Soil-3 profile is at 45 cm, SN 61425, and says explicitly that the 64 cm figure was copied from UQAM_1. The field note of 2026-08-20, which rechecked every probe location and serial number on site, records the same serial at 64 cm: 7H SN61425 (64cm). The other three depths agree in both sources (8, 16 and 32 cm, SN 61438 / 61418 / 61426).

The 2025 temperature record favours 64 cm. Fitting the annual wave's amplitude decay across the four depths gives a damping depth that, divided by √365, should equal the damping depth measured independently from the summer daily wave between 8 and 16 cm. With the deepest probe at 64 cm the two agree to 1.6 % (12.7 cm predicted, 12.9 cm observed); at 45 cm they disagree by 36 %. The 2026 season is only two-thirds complete, so its annual amplitude is biased and the same test there is inconclusive.
before.fix: Do not change the ini on the strength of the temperature test alone: settle it with a tape on the next visit and then correct whichever source is wrong. Meanwhile treat TS_4, SWC_1_4_1 and the other *_1_4_1 traces at UQAM_2 as being at an uncertain depth between 45 and 64 cm.
before.flag: The ini and the 2026-08-20 field note give different depths for the same serial number (61425). The ini's note that 45 cm replaced a value copied from UQAM_1 suggests somebody deliberately corrected it, but the field check that followed four months later recorded 64 cm. One of the two is wrong and the data lean towards 64 cm.

before.ti: Water table sensors and water probes are disconnected every winter
before.period: Every winter, from the fall removal to the spring reinstallation
before.b: At every site the CS456 pressure transducers (WTD_1_1_1) and the Eureka EasyProbe water multiprobes (water temperature, conductivity, dissolved oxygen, ORP, pH and level) are disconnected for the winter, because they get damaged when the water gets close to 0 °C. before.fix: Exclude each removal-to-reinstallation window in first stage, one dated window per winter and per sensor, rather than relying on the min/max limits to catch it. Each reinstallation changes the transducer's position, so the WTD datum has to be re-measured at every spring reinstallation and entered as a new dated currentCalibration row (see the water table caveat above); the previous season's offset does not carry over. Write the removal and reinstallation dates, and the new sensor depth, in the field note of that visit.
before.xref: The field notes record one winter removal so far: the McGill_1 EasyProbe, taken out on 2025-11-10 for the freezing risk and reinstalled on 2026-04-23. after.ti: Water table sensors and water probes are disconnected every winter
after.period: Every winter, from the fall removal to the spring reinstallation
after.b: At every site the CS456 pressure transducers (WTD_1_1_1) and the Eureka EasyProbe water multiprobes (water temperature, conductivity, dissolved oxygen, ORP, pH and level) are disconnected for the winter, because they get damaged when the water gets close to 0 °C. Whatever these channels record between the fall removal and the spring reinstallation is not a measurement of the water.
after.fix: Exclude each removal-to-reinstallation window in first stage, one dated window per winter and per sensor, rather than relying on the min/max limits to catch it. Each reinstallation changes the transducer's position, so the WTD datum has to be re-measured at every spring reinstallation and entered as a new dated currentCalibration row (see the water table caveat above); the previous season's offset does not carry over. Write the removal and reinstallation dates, and the new sensor depth, in the field note of that visit.
after.xref: The field notes record one winter removal so far: the McGill_1 EasyProbe, taken out on 2025-11-10 for the freezing risk and reinstalled on 2026-04-23. Every CS456 went in during spring 2026 (UQAM_3 on 2026-04-15, UQAM_2 from 2026-04-27, UQAM_1 on 2026-05-07, UQAM_4 on 2026-05-15, McGill_1 on 2026-05-28), so the coming winter is the first one for them. The UQAM_1 EasyProbe stayed in during the 2024–25 winter and was found frozen inside its pipe in January 2025. On 2026-11-11 the CS456 at UQAM_2, UQAM_3, UQAM_4 and McGill_1 were all still logging (water 8 to 12 °C); the UQAM_1 CS456 only logged 2026-05-07 → 05-28.

after.ti: SmartFlux Core firmware changes the EP-Summary format
after.b: After the SmartFlux2 to SmartFlux Core upgrade, the daily EP-Summary files write the header checksum (e.g. 159 at UQAM_4) where the last column used to be named CHK. Biomet.net fr_read_SmartFlux_file.m uses header names as struct fields, so MATLAB throws "Invalid field name" and fr_SmartFlux_database skips every file: all UQAM_4 flux traces are missing from the database after the upgrade. Other format changes (Fortran-style numbers such as 0.45E-02, DOY with 4 decimals) are harmless. Raw data are complete (36000 samples per half hour, LI-7200 signal and flow continuous, checked Oct 20 to Nov 4).
after.fix: Use the patched fr_read_SmartFlux_file.m (EC-live-diagnostics\outputs\2026-11-04_UQAM_4_SmartFluxCore). It detects each file's format from the last header field, so old and new files load together; failed files are not marked processed and reload on the next database update. Deploy it before rerunning UQAM_1.
after.xref: Field notes agree: UQAM_4 visit 2026-10-30 (on site 10:23 to 11:02 EDT, i.e. 09:23 EST in the database) records the firmware upgrade. The UQAM_1 visit of 2026-11-06 records "Smartflux 2 SN00780 upgraded to SmartFlux Core", so UQAM_1 is affected from that date too; this was not part of the original diagnosis.

after.resolved: Marked as dealt with on 2026-11-11. The patched fr_read_SmartFlux_file.m reads both formats: checked in the database on 2026-11-11, UQAM_4 fluxes load for 340 of 340 half hours from Oct 30 to Nov 6, and UQAM_1 for 227 of 262 after its Nov 6 upgrade.

after.ti: CSAT3B SN 1892 failing in the cold, sonic temperature biased
after.b: From about 2026-09-18 SmartFlux (AIU-2496) produced no flux for most half hours below roughly 9 to 12 °C. On cool nights 60 to 75 % of the 20 Hz records were -9999 (no sonic record) and the rest flagged (diagnostic values 26, 27, 8, 9, 19: acquiring, high amplitude, high delta C), independently of humidity. In August the same head worked down to 3 to 6 °C, so it degraded. Its sonic temperature also ran about +2.0 °C above the expected virtual temperature all season (SN 1898: +0.1 °C), a speed-of-sound error of about 1.2 m/s pointing to a path length or transducer timing fault. After the swap to SN 1898, 98 to 100 % of dry half hours give flux down to -8 °C, with flags only in rain. SmartFlux EddyPro does not filter on the anemometer diagnostic (used_records = file_records, col_diag_anem = -1), so flagged records entered the fluxes. EP summaries are empty or missing for Oct 12, 13, 14, 16 and 17 (raw .ghg files exist).
after.fix: Reprocess 2026-09-18 → 2026-10-23 from the raw .ghg files with the anemometer diagnostic filter on, or discard those fluxes. Do not use SN 1892 sonic temperature (Aug 1 → Oct 23) as an air temperature. Rerun EddyPro for Oct 12, 13, 14, 16, 17.
after.xref: Field notes agree: the 2026-10-23 visit records SN 1892 swapped for SN 1898 at 11:29 with no visible damage.
after.flag: The same visit is entered twice: note 145 (2026-10-23) and note 139, dated 2026-10-26 but whose text says Friday, October 23, 2026. The data confirm Oct 23. Also open: whether the sonic cable was changed with the head.

after.ti: Pluvio2 weighing gauge invalid, main-logger Pluvio column is a constant zero
after.b: The OTT Pluvio2 400 (SN 454900) on its own CR1000X (LoggerNet station LSP_pluvio, files UQAM_1_Pluvio_Met_30m.*) reported status 256 (weight below minimum) in every half hour. Aug 3 → Sep 18: 5 to 12 mm/day of false accumulation, mostly on dry warm mornings (Aug 19 → Sep 18: about 279 mm against about 77 mm in the tipping buckets). After Sep 18: flat zero, real rain missed (Oct 13: 19 mm). Over-range spikes (status 785, Bucket_RT_Max up to 1250 mm) on Aug 31, Sep 20, Oct 18. No Pluvio files for Aug 10 18:30 → Aug 19 00:00. Separately, the main logger never polled a Pluvio, so its P_2_1_1_Tot (Jul 2024 onward) is a constant 0 and its Pluvio_* columns are NaN: not a measurement. The spare installed on Nov 6 reports status 0, about 116 mm empty bucket with no thermal drift, and agrees with the tipping buckets on Nov 8 and Nov 10.
after.fix: Mark all Pluvio variables bad from 2026-08-03 11:00 to 2026-11-06 13:00 and use the UQAM_1 tipping bucket P_1_1_1 for that period (it agrees with McGill_1: 137 vs 132 mm, Aug 19 → Nov 4). Drop P_2_1_1_Tot from the main-logger traces. Data from 2026-11-06 13:30 are good but provisional until a 1 L water test. The accumulation reset (455.16 → 0), the Bucket_RT jump (1.25 → about 116 mm) and the RECORD restart at the swap are not rain.

after.ti: SnowVUE channel shared with a CS650, soil heat flux plates disturbed
after.b: CS650 SN69260 was wired to 9H, the channel reserved for the SnowVUE, until it was moved to 17H (_5_1_1) on 2026-10-15. While they shared the channel, the snow depth record is meaningless (D_SNOW 1.9 to 18 m) and the CS650 itself was never logged. Some soil heat flux plates were also found uncovered and even upside down and were reinstalled that day. The CS650 profile (8, 16, 32, 64 cm) was installed on 2026-10-15. SWC_1_1_1 was a horizontal replica on 1H until 2026-10-15 and is the top of the profile (SN 69255) since then, so expect a level shift at the move.
after.fix: Discard D_SNOW and DI_SnowVUE from the start of the record (2026-08-06) to 2026-10-15, and soil heat flux over the same period (the ini only marks it as questionable). SWC_5_1_1 and TS_5_1_1 start on 2026-10-15. Set the SnowVUE height to 4.00 m from 2026-10-15.

after.ti: Storm outage and LI-7200 head change
after.b: On 2026-09-04 the solar panels were found blown down and the system was shut down except for the sonic anemometer until four panels were reconnected on 2026-09-11; the SmartFlux was off, so no fluxes were computed at all. The LI-7700 had already stopped producing CH4 fluxes on 2026-08-31. On 2026-10-09 the LI-7200 head 72H-1201 (damaged thermocouples) was replaced by 72H-1231, running on the old AIU-2491 with the 72H-1231 coefficients uploaded (AIU-2532 did not work). The damaged inlet thermocouple (t_in) logged values of 11,000 to 36,000 from 2026-07-04 04:30 to 07-08 and from 2026-08-19 to the swap.
after.fix: Expect no fluxes at all (H included) 2026-09-04 13:30 → 2026-09-11 14:30, and no CH4 2026-08-31 07:30 → 2026-09-11. For the t_in windows, recompute CO2 and H2O from the raw files with the cell temperature from t_out only, or flag them. The metadata after 2026-10-09 match 72H-1231 (checked on a 2026-11-10 file).

after.ti: Third-stage wake filter uses the wrong north offset at five sites
after.b:
The third stage removes fluxes when the wind comes from within ±30° of the back of the sonic, using northOffset in each site's config.yml. Those values do not match the sonic north offsets in the SmartFlux metadata:
  • McGill_1: 285 in config.yml, 290 in the metadata
  • UQAM_1: 285, 285 (correct)
  • UQAM_2: 285, 264
  • UQAM_3: 285, 332
  • UQAM_4: 218, 213
  • UQAM_5: 0, 267
So at UQAM_2, UQAM_3 and UQAM_5 the filter removes good data from one sector and keeps data from behind the tower.
after.fix: Set northOffset in each config.yml to the sonic north offset in the metadata (UQAM_2 264, UQAM_3 332, UQAM_4 213, UQAM_5 267, McGill_1 290), then rerun third stage. config.yml takes one value per site, so it cannot follow the boom movements: for UQAM_2 2025-12-01 03:30 → 2025-12-17 14:30 and UQAM_3 2026-03-17 02:00 → 2026-03-27 12:30 (pn9, pn11) the wake filter points the wrong way. Exclude or rerun those windows instead.
after.xref: Sonic north offsets read from the metadata of the latest raw file of each site (2026-10-31 for UQAM_1, 2026-11-10 for the others): 290, 285, 264, 332, 213 and 267. The metadata value does not change during the boom movements: the UQAM_2 file of 2025-12-10, in the middle of the boom window, still says 264. config.yml files read on GitHub (commit 88fcb05).
